name: Year 11 Genetics – Key Terms and Definitions

cards.definition: The molecule that stores genetic information in living organisms.
A section of DNA that contains instructions for making a protein.
A long, organised structure of DNA wrapped around proteins called histones.
The basic building block of DNA, made of a sugar, phosphate and nitrogenous base.
The twisted-ladder shape of DNA.
One of the four DNA bases: adenine, thymine, cytosine or guanine.
A DNA base that pairs with thymine.
A DNA base that pairs with adenine.
A DNA base that pairs with guanine.
A DNA base that pairs with cytosine.
The matching of DNA bases: A with T, and C with G.
Proteins that DNA wraps around to help organise chromosomes.
The specific position of a gene on a chromosome.
An alternative version of a gene.
The combination of alleles an organism has for a particular gene.
The observable characteristics of an organism.
An allele that is expressed when at least one copy is present.
An allele that is expressed only when two copies are present.
Having two identical alleles for a gene.
Having two different alleles for a gene.
Having two dominant alleles (e.g. BB).
Having two recessive alleles (e.g. bb).
Having one dominant and one recessive allele (e.g. Bb).
A matching pair of chromosomes, one inherited from each parent.
A reproductive cell, such as a sperm or egg cell.
A cell containing one set of chromosomes.
A cell containing two sets of chromosomes.
Cell division that produces four genetically different haploid cells.
Cell division that produces two genetically identical cells.
The exchange of DNA between homologous chromosomes during Prophase I of meiosis.
The random arrangement of homologous chromosome pairs during meiosis.
The joining of two gametes to form a zygote.
Differences in genetic information between individuals of the same species.
A change in the DNA sequence.
A mutation that occurs in a body cell.
A mutation that occurs in a reproductive cell and may be passed to offspring.
The process of copying genetic information from DNA into messenger RNA.
The process of using messenger RNA instructions to build a protein.
A molecule made from amino acids that performs many functions in an organism.
A diagram showing how a characteristic is inherited through generations of a family.
A diagram used to predict possible offspring genotypes from a genetic cross.
A cross used to determine the genotype of an organism showing a dominant phenotype.
An individual with one recessive allele who does not show the recessive characteristic.
An organised image of an individual's chromosomes.
A condition where a cell has an abnormal number of chromosomes.
Having three copies of a particular chromosome instead of two.
A genetic condition caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21.
A chromosome condition commonly involving XXY sex chromosomes.
A chromosome condition involving a single X chromosome (monosomy X).
A genetic condition caused by an extra copy of chromosome 13.
A genetic condition caused by an extra copy of chromosome 18.
Chromosomes involved in determining biological sex; commonly XX or XY in humans.
The first cell formed when two gametes join during fertilisation.
All the genes and alleles present in a population.
